title: Reverse a String
lesson:
## Strings

a string is just text. wrap anything in quotes — that's a string.

```python
name    = "Alice"
message = "hello, world!"
empty   = ""
```

single quotes work too. `'Alice'` and `"Alice"` are the same thing.

---

### reading one character at a time

imagine a string as a row of boxes. each box holds one character.

python numbers the boxes starting at **0**, not 1.

```python
s = "Python"
#    P  y  t  h  o  n
#    0  1  2  3  4  5

s[0]   # 'P'  — first box
s[-1]  # 'n'  — last box (negatives count from the end)
s[-2]  # 'o'  — second to last
```

> counting starts at 0. always. this trips up beginners constantly.

---

### grabbing a chunk (slicing)

`s[start:stop]` gives you characters from start up to — but **not including** — stop.

```python
s = "Hello"

s[0:3]   # 'Hel'   — positions 0, 1, 2 (stops before 3)
s[1:]    # 'ello'  — from 1 to the end
s[:3]    # 'Hel'   — from start to position 2
s[::-1]  # 'olleH' — reversed (step -1 = go backwards)
```

> the stop number is never included. `s[0:3]` gives 3 characters, not 4.

---

### putting variables inside text — f-strings

put `f` before the quote, then use `{variable}` to drop anything in:

```python
name = "Alice"
age  = 25

f"hello, {name}!"           # 'hello, Alice!'
f"you are {age} years old." # 'you are 25 years old.'
f"next year: {age + 1}"     # 'next year: 26'  — math works too!
```

---

### the most useful string tools

```python
"hello".upper()             # 'HELLO'
"HELLO".lower()             # 'hello'
"  hi  ".strip()            # 'hi'    — removes edge spaces
"hello".replace("l", "r")  # 'herro'
"a,b,c".split(",")          # ['a', 'b', 'c']
len("hello")                # 5
```

> you can't change a character inside a string. `s[0] = "H"` will crash. build a new string instead: `"H" + s[1:]`
description:
Write a function `reverse_string(s)` that returns the string reversed.

**Examples:**
```python
reverse_string("hello")   # 'olleh'
reverse_string("Python")  # 'nohtyP'
reverse_string("a")       # 'a'
reverse_string("")        # ''
```

**Hint:** Python slicing with a step of `-1` reverses a sequence: `s[::-1]`
